title: I Followed the Parking-Garage Elevator Override Through Three Levels After They Cut the Attendant

parts.text: They cut the night garage attendant and posted an elevator override on the P2 ticket machine. I was thirty-five, facilities contractor, holding a badge that still opened one stair. At 10:22 p.m. the code opened P2 and, I found, the car to P3. Temporary, the vendor said. I photographed the ticket slip, both levels, the time. Then a sedan I did not recognize used the same numbers toward P4.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The unrecognized sedan just used the ticket-machine code toward P4.

social.video_title: They posted the elevator override on the tickets — Part 1/3
social.description: Night attendant cut, a ticket code, a sedan toward P4. Would you have followed the car?

parts.text: I followed on foot with the stills. P4's panel took the same four digits. The driver palmed a duffel that was not a parking errand I could see from the light. I was still thirty-five, still contracted, suddenly the only witness with a timestamp. I messaged safety the panel still and stayed in the camera cone. The driver looked at the cone, then at the last panel on P5.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He is at the P5 panel; safety now has the still.

social.video_title: The same four digits opened P4 — Part 2/3
social.description: A duffel off-errand, a camera cone, P5 next. Safety has the still. Do you stay in the cone?

parts.text: Safety locked P5 from the booth. The driver left the duffel and the code on a sticky. Morning recoded all five levels. The vendor who called it temporary lost the contract. I keep a badge that opens one stair. Ticket machines print tickets now, not keys. The garage at 10:22 sounds like a garage, which is to say concrete and nobody's four digits.

social.video_title: Morning recoded all five levels — Part 3/3
social.description: Sticky code, a lost contract, machines that print tickets. Was temporary ever five levels?
